# Reading as a sequence

A page unfolds over time. The reader finds a title, follows an opening paragraph and gradually learns which details deserve attention. Typography supports that sequence through small, repeatable choices: the width of a line, the distance between paragraphs and the contrast between a heading and the words beneath it.

This document gives those choices somewhere to meet. Read several paragraphs before changing a value, then return to the same passage. A setting that looks pleasing in a short sample may feel very different after a full screen of continuous prose. These examples are demonstrations rather than research findings [@sample-notes].

> The task of a reading page is to make it easy to continue, and equally easy to find the way back.

A quotation interrupts the main voice without leaving the argument. Its border, indentation and line spacing should make that relationship visible. A footnote offers a smaller departure, allowing the reader to follow a detail and return.[^reading]

[^reading]: This is an illustrative note. It tests the size, spacing and link treatment of supporting text in the exported theme.

# Methods {#methods}

## Compare the same passage

Choose a baseline, adjust one property and compare the result. The page should retain a clear hierarchy when the viewport changes, when a long title wraps or when a reader switches to a dark palette.

1. Start with the body font, its size and its line height.
2. Adjust the reading column and the space between paragraphs.
3. Compare section headings, quotations and notes with the main text.

::: {.callout-note}
## Keep the context visible

The preview includes Quarto's generated structure and Bootstrap theme. Your exported CSS is applied after that baseline, so you can inspect how the two work together.
:::

## Record the settings

A small table can carry the practical details without interrupting the prose for long.

| Property | Example | What to inspect |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Reading width | 68ch | Line length |
| Body size | 18px | Comfort at normal zoom |
| Line height | 1.65 | Separation between lines |

: An illustrative comparison sheet.

```css
article p {
  margin-block-end: 1.2em;
}
```

Code has its own rhythm. Keep indentation and punctuation distinct, while allowing the surrounding explanation to retain its ordinary measure. Inline expressions such as `margin-block-end` should remain legible inside a sentence.

# Discussion

A website adds a second kind of structure. Navigation identifies the publication, a table of contents describes the current document and the footer marks its end. These elements can share colors and type with the article while keeping their own spacing and dimensions.

The final check is a continuous reading pass. Move from the opening paragraph to the notes, inspect a narrow viewport, then compare light and dark. The value of a theme lies in how consistently these parts support the text.
